Your troops have marched to a local outpost, and the master strategist has resolved all obstacles: build a military fortress to secure the border, establish a marketplace to enrich the army's coffers, set up an administrative hall to settle the populace, or open a post road to connect all directions. What is your will?
The outpost market has taken shape. Merchants gather, and requests come to expand the marketplace to broaden revenue. Grant the request, and taxes grow richer; delay it, and things remain unchanged.

The outpost's relay station has connected to the post road. The stationmaster requests permission to add more relay horses and improve the roads, so marching troops move faster, scouts range further, and losses shrink. Grant the request, and mobility improves; delay it, and things remain unchanged.

The outpost has become a military garrison. The general in command requests permission to raise funds and grain to further fortify the ramparts, strengthening its military might. Grant the request, and its blades grow sharper; delay it, and things remain unchanged.

The outpost's administrative hall has taken initial shape. Advisors petition to expand the offices to settle the people's hearts and improve governance. Grant the request, and order grows firmer; delay it, and things remain unchanged.
